items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And this is when Snooky Young came back to the band and Lockjaw Davis and I.

ctx.x: So you ran and got your horn.

Yeah. I went to the north side. We lived up on North Philadelphia near the ballpark up there near the stadium on North 27th Street. I got my horn and came back and, coming from Dizzy, you know I was playing pretty strong by then, you know? So yeah, I sitted in and played music and played solos that was really outasight. And so Count Basie called me back to his dressing room and said, “well we’re getting ready to go to England in the next five days, and we’d like to take you along with us, could you make it?” I…
I want you to finish your story about the Basie band when you joined that, and then we’re going to come back and tell a little bit about Joe.

items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Trombones; Henry Coker, Al Grey, Benny Powell…[shoo] killers.

ctx.x: Trombones; Henry Coker, Al Grey, Benny Powell…[shoo] killers. Reeds; Marshal Royal, Frank Wes—[shoo] love Frank, Eddie ―Lockjaw‖ Davis, Frank Foster, Charles Fowlkes. And then rhythm section; Freddie Green, bass; Eddie Jones, of course Count Basie on piano, and Sonny Payne on drums.

items.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Wendell Culley and myself was the trumpet section. Henry Coker, Al Grey and Benny Powell were the trombone section. And the reeds was Marshall Royal, baritone was Charlie Fowlkes, Frank Wess, Frank Foster, and Billy Mitchell.

ctx.x: What was the first fast company you came back into?

Count Basie. And that was when he was the hottest. I mean his next trip around, “The Comeback.” Joe Williams was in the band then, you know? And oh, that was, Thad Jones, Joe Newman, Wendell Culley and myself was the trumpet section. Henry Coker, Al Grey and Benny Powell were the trombone section. And the reeds was Marshall Royal, baritone was Charlie Fowlkes, Frank Wess, Frank Foster, and Billy Mitchell. Billy Mitchell.
